title: p0290
universal_lens: The adjudication of simultaneous infractions constitutes a hierarchical temporal filtering operator. By imposing a strict partial order on event timestamps and assigning precedence weights to observer classes, the system resolves combinatorial state collisions into a singular, deterministic penalty projection.
gsi_mapping: GSI models officiating as a multi-sensor Bayesian network. The Umpire and Linesman act as stochastic detectors with distinct likelihood functions. When detection events collide temporally, conformal inference applies hierarchical priors to select the maximum a posteriori penalty state.
gse_mapping: In GSE, play-state transitions are governed by a priority queue. Simultaneous foul signals trigger a collision resolution protocol. The engine evaluates temporal deltas; if indeterminate, it executes a hierarchical fallback, ensuring a single, valid state mutation per scrimmage.

primitives.name: Chronological Infraction Selector
primitives.verbatim_quote: 276 FOOTBALL case the Linesman and Umpire each signal a foul against the same side during the same scrimmage (unnecessary roughness excepted) only one penalty shall be given, viz.: that for the foul committed first.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t_i: timestamp of infraction i (seconds), P: penalty space, \delta t: temporal resolution threshold (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Infractions possess discrete, measurable onset times within the continuous flow of the scrimmage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities arise when \Delta t approaches zero or falls below human/mechanical perception thresholds, rendering chronological ordering impossible.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to packet collision resolution in time-division multiplexing networks, where earliest arrival dictates processing priority.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in referee-reported foul timestamps across multiple camera angles.

primitives.name: Authority Weighted Resolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: In case it is impossible to say which foul occurred first the penalty shall be exacted only for the foul noted by the Umpire.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: O_k: observer class k (Referee, Umpire, Linesman), w_k: authority weight (dimensionless), F_{k}: foul detected by O_k
primitives.assumptions: A static, universally agreed-upon hierarchy exists among officiating positions (w_{umpire} > w_{linesman}).
primitives.breakdown_regime: System failure occurs if the highest-weighted observer fails to detect any infractions while lower-tier observers register multiple.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to consensus algorithms in distributed systems utilizing static node reputation scores to break ties during network partitions.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of Umpire overrides relative to total simultaneous foul calls.

primitives.name: Functional Equivalence Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the above cases a foul called by the Referee shall be judged the same as if called by the Linesman.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \phi: mapping function from Observer Role to Authority Weight, R: Referee, L: Linesman
primitives.assumptions: Specific rule subsets allow dynamic reassignment of authority weights based on contextual jurisdiction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ambiguity emerges if the mapped role conflicts with the primary hierarchical fallback defined in other rule articles.

layer2.mapping: Represents a context-dependent override matrix in GSE state machines, dynamically altering the precedence queue based on play phase.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of successful Referee-to-Linesman functional mappings during complex multi-foul plays.

The provided excerpts define a rigorous state-reduction mechanism for concurrent adversarial events. Mathematically, we model a scrimmage as a continuous time interval containing a set of potential infraction events $E = \{e_1, e_2, ..., e_n\}$, each possessing an onset timestamp $t_i$ and an associated observer $O_j$. The primary operator, `temporal_precedence_filter`, seeks to minimize the cardinality of applied penalties by selecting $\arg \min_{e \in E} t_i$. This assumes a perfectly resolved timeline. However, physical reality introduces measurement noise; when $|t_i - t_j| < \epsilon$, the chronological ordering becomes undefined. Here, the system transitions to the `hierarchical_observer_fallback`. We assign scalar weights $w(O)$ to each official, establishing a strict total order over the observer classes. If temporal sorting fails, the penalty is determined by $\arg \max_{O} w(O)$ among those who registered the simultaneous events. Furthermore, the `observer_role_isomorphism` introduces a dynamic layer, asserting that under specific conditions, the weight vector is transformed such that $w(Referee) \rightarrow w(Linesman)$. This creates a composite decision surface where the final game state is a non-linear function of both event timing and spatial-jurisdictional topology. The dualities lie between absolute chronology and structural authority. Failure modes manifest primarily at the singularity of simultaneous detection ($\Delta t \rightarrow 0$), forcing reliance entirely on the potentially subjective hierarchical priors, thereby introducing systemic bias if the higher-weighted observer possesses inferior geometric vantage points.

The rules implicitly model the cognitive limits of human perception, acknowledging that perfect temporal resolution is unattainable without technological augmentation.
